$comment: Task 1 deliverable for CLAUDE_HYDROFUSION_IMPLEMENTATION_TASKS_20261115.md. Updated in 1.1.0 (independent-review correction) to synchronize split_rule, masks, and the discharge_valid caveat with the actual Task 2 implementation and its own correction cycle -- the 1.0.0 version of this schema had drifted from both the corrected markdown and the fixed code. See hydrofusion_forecast_contract.md for the prose rationale behind every field below.

horizon.note: Prospectively fixed. Other horizons are future work, not a silent grid.

availability.note: latency_model must be set to a non-idealized value explicitly before any run is described as operational. availability_index(h) = h + 1 + latency_hours.

reserved_period_seal.note: Duplicated literal, matching this codebase's existing per-file convention (no shared header exports it).

package_scope.note: No package-kind flag exists at the loader level (GisToOhqPackageConfig / loadHydroPackageTensors); enforcement is caller-side only, via holdout_mode_default=false and the reserved_period_seal checks above.

domain_guards.max_representable_x_note: A finite, integer-valued double can still exceed int64_t's representable range (~9.223e18); static_cast<int64_t> of such a value is undefined behavior, not merely a large number. Checked explicitly before every x-to-int64 cast (HourlyIndex construction and runPersistenceBenchmark's own origin loop), with margin below int64_t's actual max so no double-rounding ambiguity falls near the boundary.
domain_guards.origin_domain_checked_before_arithmetic: buildSample validates originHour is in [0, max_representable_x - 1] before computing targetHour = originHour + 1, not after.
domain_guards.derived_feature_finiteness: Every individual discharge/met value read is checked finite and (where physically meaningful) nonnegative, but finite inputs do not guarantee finite derived results -- trailing-window sums/means/variances and the two difference-based features (q_last_hourly_change, q_past_slope_6h) are independently re-checked for finiteness after computation; a non-finite derived value voids predictor_availability_mask for the whole sample rather than being stored.

discharge_memory_group.validity_flag_caveat: discharge_valid is caller-supplied in this prototype. The prototype does NOT trust it alone -- every read additionally requires std::isfinite and >= 0 on the value itself, independent of the flag -- but the flag's semantic claim of genuine NATIVE (non-interpolated) support is unproven here; that proof is Task 4's responsibility once a real GisToOhq loader adapter populates this field. A boolean name alone does not establish native support.

features.name: q_past_slope_6h
features.note: This prototype's specific fixed choice of window for 'a simple past-only slope'.

meteorological_at_origin_group.validity_flag: all_forcings_valid (plus each field's own per-field validity flag)

excluded_by_design: any snow/spring regime feature (not established for Sligo, not borrowed by analogy)

requires: every row read by discharge_memory_group (o-71..o, as applicable per feature) exists, is discharge_valid, AND carries a finite, nonnegative value (the flag alone is not trusted numerically)
every row read shares the same segment_id as o (no cross-gap lookback)

row o is all_forcings_valid for meteorological_at_origin_group AND every one of its six fields is finite, with precipitation/wind_speed/solar/pet/relative_humidity additionally nonnegative (temperature_c has no such domain constraint)

every DERIVED feature (q_trailing_mean_*, q_trailing_var_*, q_last_hourly_change, q_past_slope_6h) is itself finite -- finite inputs do not guarantee finite derived arithmetic (e.g. a trailing mean over large-but-finite values can overflow); a non-finite derived value voids the mask even when every input it was built from was individually valid
row (o+1) exists, is discharge_valid, and carries a finite, nonnegative value (non-interpolated observation; same numeric-vs-flag independence as above)

masks.policy: Both masks applied identically before training loss and before scoring, for every arm (persistence, direct-log-Q, log-residual).

segment_id_rule.derived_from: actual chronological gaps (integer hour value of x; non-finite/non-integer x rejected; duplicate/non-monotonic x rejected)

production_path_semantics.operates_on: torch tensors and windowed-sequence array positions (train_end/validation_end/test_end are sequence-array indices, resolved from x via resolveTestEndSequenceCount's endpoint lookup)
production_path_semantics.boundary_semantics: half-open; train_end excluded from train (first index of validation); validation_end excluded from validation (first index of test); test_end excluded from test (position >= test_end is beyond_test_end)

prototype_adapter_semantics.independence_note: This is a narrowly-scoped, independent, torch-free adapter -- NOT a call into configuredChronologicalSplit, which requires torch tensors and sequence-array positions that do not exist at this builder's raw-per-row granularity. The 1.0.0 version of this schema incorrectly stated resolved_via as configuredChronologicalSplit 'only'; this was inaccurate and is corrected here.
prototype_adapter_semantics.operates_on: raw exported-x values directly (train_end_x/validation_end_x/test_end_x are inclusive x-coordinate cutoffs, not sequence-array indices)
prototype_adapter_semantics.cutoff_semantics: a row whose x equals the cutoff is the last row included in that partition (x <= cutoff), equivalent in effect to the production path's half-open sequence-position bound but expressed directly in x-space
prototype_adapter_semantics.parity_verification: checked against resolveTestEndSequenceCountFromSorted (dataset/resolve_test_end_x.h) -- the same pure, torch-free core the production path itself calls -- in test_hydrofusion_feature_builder.cpp's testPartitionForXParityWithProduction, including across a gapped sequence. Parity is verified, not assumed.
prototype_adapter_semantics.required_cutoff_ordering: 0 <= train_end_x < validation_end_x < test_end_x < seal_start_x, enforced by validateSplitCutoffs() BEFORE any sample work in runPersistenceBenchmark -- an out-of-order or non-strict set of cutoffs throws std::invalid_argument rather than silently producing a nonsensical partition assignment

split_rule.sample_assignment: a sample (origin=o, target=o+1) is assigned to split S iff both o and o+1 resolve to the same partition S under the prototype adapter; otherwise the sample is discarded entirely, never partially assigned
split_rule.historical_context_exception: discharge-memory lookup rows (o-71..o) may fall in an earlier split than the sample's own assigned split (purely causal, not a future label)
split_rule.forbidden: for a train-split sample, target_x > train_end_x (strictly past the cutoff) is forbidden; target_x == train_end_x is allowed, consistent with the inclusive exported-x cutoff (train_end_x itself is the last x value included in train)
